title: Scratches and nail care for newborns
summary: Face scratches from sharp nails are common. Gentle trimming and mittens can help.
whatsNormal:
Newborn nails are thin but sharp, and babies wave their hands near their face.

• Small red scratch marks on the face usually heal quickly without scarring
• Trim nails when baby is calm or sleeping, press finger pad down to see nail edge clearly
• Use baby nail scissors or a soft emery board; skip adult clippers if you are nervous
• Cotton mittens or long sleeves for sleep can reduce scratches short term

Scratches on the face without other symptoms are not an emergency.
watchFor: Scratch becoming red, swollen, warm, or with pus
Many deep scratches daily despite trimming
Bleeding that will not stop with gentle pressure
callDoctorIf: Signs of skin infection around a scratch
Eye redness, swelling, or discharge after a near-eye scratch
You nicked the skin while trimming and it will not stop bleeding
You want a nurse to show nail trimming in clinic, many offices will
